questions.stem: Translate into English: Ich mag Hunde, aber ich mag keine Spinnen.
markscheme: B1: I like dogs
B1: but I do not like spiders (keine makes the sentence negative)
questions.modelAnswer: Mögen means to like: Ich mag Hunde is I like dogs. The negative with mögen uses kein: ich mag keine Spinnen is I do not like spiders. So the whole sentence is: I like dogs, but I do not like spiders.

questions.stem: Complete each sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets: (a) Ich ___ gern Tennis. (spielen) (b) ___ du gern Musik? (hören)
markscheme: B1: (a) spiele — ich takes the ending -e (stem spiel- + e)
B1: (b) Hörst — du takes the ending -st, and the verb comes first in a yes/no question
questions.modelAnswer: (a) Ich spiele gern Tennis. Regular verbs take the stem (spiel-) plus -e with ich. (b) Hörst du gern Musik? With du the ending is -st (hörst), and in a yes/no question the verb comes first, before the subject du.

questions.stem: What do you say in German (a) to a friend on their birthday? (b) to a classmate who is ill?
markscheme: B1: (a) Alles Gute zum Geburtstag! (accept Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum Geburtstag!)
B1: (b) Gute Besserung!
questions.modelAnswer: (a) On a birthday you say Alles Gute zum Geburtstag! — all the best for your birthday (Herzlichen Glückwunsch! also works for congratulations). (b) To someone who is ill you say Gute Besserung! — literally good improvement, the German get well soon.

questions.stem: Translate into English: Ich möchte den blauen Pullover kaufen, aber er kostet fünfundvierzig Euro. Das ist zu teuer!
markscheme: B1: I would like to buy the blue jumper
B1: but it costs forty-five euros
B1: that is too expensive
questions.modelAnswer: Ich möchte ... kaufen is I would like to buy (möchte is the polite would like), and den blauen Pullover is the blue jumper — der Pullover becomes den in the accusative. Fünfundvierzig is 45 (five-and-forty), so er kostet fünfundvierzig Euro is it costs forty-five euros. Teuer means expensive, so the last sentence is: That is too expensive!

questions.stem: Translate into German: (a) I was in Vienna in the summer. (b) The weather was great!
markscheme: B1: (a) Ich war im Sommer in Wien (ich war = I was, past of sein; Wien = Vienna)
B1: (b) Das Wetter war super / toll
questions.modelAnswer: (a) Ich war im Sommer in Wien. The past tense of sein is ich war (I was), Vienna is Wien in German, and in the summer is im Sommer. (b) Das Wetter war super! (or war toll) — das Wetter is neuter and singular, so it also takes war.

questions.stem: A German exchange student is cooking with you and does not understand the recipe. Write these instructions in German using the du-imperative: (a) Take two eggs! (b) Cut the onion! (c) Bake the cake for 30 minutes!
markscheme: B1: (a) Nimm zwei Eier! (nehmen drops the -st of du nimmst and keeps the vowel change)
B1: (b) Schneide die Zwiebel! (verb stem, verb first)
B1: (c) Backe den Kuchen 30 Minuten! (der Kuchen becomes den in the accusative)
questions.modelAnswer: (a) Nimm zwei Eier! For a du-command you take the du-form and drop the -st: du nimmst becomes Nimm! (b) Schneide die Zwiebel! — du schneidest loses its -st and the verb jumps to first position. (c) Backe den Kuchen 30 Minuten! — der Kuchen is masculine and becomes den in the accusative. In every imperative the verb comes first in the sentence.

questions.stem: Translate into German: (a) I am looking forward to the party. (b) Lisa is sad because her cat is ill.
markscheme: B1: (a) Ich freue mich auf die Party — reflexive mich plus auf for a future event
B1: (b) Lisa ist traurig (correct vocabulary and adjective without an ending after sein)
B1: weil ihre Katze krank ist — after weil the verb ist goes to the end of the clause
questions.modelAnswer: (a) Ich freue mich auf die Party. Sich freuen is reflexive, so ich needs mich, and a future event (the party has not happened yet) takes auf, not über. (b) Lisa ist traurig, weil ihre Katze krank ist. After sein the adjective traurig takes no ending, and weil sends the conjugated verb to the very end: weil ihre Katze krank ist.

questions.stem: Your German friend Ben has invited you to his birthday party on Saturday. Write a short reply in German (three to five sentences): thank him for the invitation, say clearly whether you can come, and add one more detail (for example a present, what you will bring, or how much you are looking forward to it).
markscheme: B1: thanks Ben for the invitation, e.g. Danke für die Einladung (zu deiner Party)
B1: clearly accepts or politely declines, e.g. Ja, ich komme gern / Leider kann ich nicht kommen
B1: one further correct, relevant sentence, e.g. Ich habe ein Geschenk für dich / Ich freue mich schon auf die Party
questions.modelAnswer: Danke für die Einladung zu deiner Party, Ben! Ja, ich komme sehr gern. Ich habe ein Geschenk für dich. Ich freue mich schon auf die Party. Bis Samstag! — This reply thanks Ben (Danke für die Einladung), accepts clearly (ich komme sehr gern), and adds two correct details: a present (ein Geschenk für dich) and looking forward with the reflexive phrase Ich freue mich schon. An equally valid answer could decline politely: Danke für die Einladung, aber leider kann ich nicht kommen, weil ich krank bin. Gute Party und alles Gute zum Geburtstag!
